Title: Didi is Bengal's 'Dada' - Rediff.com India News
Home  » News » Didi is West Bengal's 'Dada'. # Didi is West Bengal's 'Dada'. **Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress overcame the might of the BJP and is all set to be CM for a third term.**. IMAGE: TMC supremo and West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee after trends show her party's win in Kolkata. Belying all expectations, the Trinamool Congress was headed Sunday for a landslide victory in assembly elections, overcoming the might of the Bharatiya Janata Party after a bitter campaign that had turned into a virtual duel between Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. "It's a victory for Bengal's people it's Banglar joy' (Bengal's victory)," Banerjee told her party workers, though her own victory from Nandigram seemed in doubt with conflicting reports of her loss by a narrow margin and a recount, neither of which were confirmed by the Election Commission. Banerjee, set to be chief minister for a third term, however, stopped celebrations by her party workers and indicated that her first priority after the victory would be "combatting the pandemic" which has been running amok in the state. The TMC's main rival, the BJP was stymied in its ambition of winning the state. The actual results were a bitter let down for the BJP as Prime Minister Modi had staked his prestige in declaring his party was set to win over 200 seats after the first few phases of the unprecedented eight-phase election. IMAGE: TMC supremo and West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee vists Kalighat Temple after her party's win. Modi and his Home Minister Amit Shah campaigned extensively throughout the state spending almost every other day of a one-and-a-half month long bruising campaign trying to breach the Trinamool Congress's fortress Bengal. IMAGE: TMC supporters celebrate the party's victory during the election result day for the West Bengal Assembly election, in Kolkata. The prime minister's repeated taunts of "Didi, O Didi" in his speeches too did not go down well in a state where women traditionally enjoyed a high social and economic status and where women remained a major vote bank for the TMC.

Title: 'Khela Ho Gaya': Influencer Mimics Mamata Banerjee As TMC Trails, BJP Leads In Bengal Polls | Times Now
# 'Khela Ho Gaya': Influencer Mimics Mamata Banerjee As TMC Trails, BJP Leads In Bengal Polls. ## A video of influencer and mimicry artist Ratan Ranjan impersonating West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has gone viral amid early election counting trends showing BJP in the lead over TMC. As early counting trends emerged, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) appeared to be comfortably ahead of the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) in West Bengal. Amid this, a social media influencer and mimicry artist, Ratan Ranjan, has gone viral for his satirical impersonation of West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. In a video shared by ANI, the influencer can be seen dressed in a saree similar to Mamata Banerjee’s signature white-and-blue attire, complete with mannerisms and gestures closely resembling the Chief Minister. He is seen imitating her speaking style, facial expressions, and public address tone, which has contributed to the clip gaining rapid traction across social media platforms. In the clip, he can be heard delivering a satirical monologue that references election trends and political slogans. He says, “Khela ho gaya hai Bengal mein. The Hindu has risen in Bengal this time. People of Bengal said that they do not want Didi this time, that they want Amit Dada and Modi Dada. Modi ji went to Bengal and had ‘jhalmuri’. He had ‘jhalmuri’ and snatched away my seat. I have lost my chair. Give me my chair back, I won’t give it up. I have lost, but I won’t give up my chair; I will run away with it.”. While many users found the mimicry humorous and viewed it as political satire, others debated the appropriateness of impersonating public figures in such a manner, especially during sensitive electoral counting phases. Meanwhile, as per the Election Commission of India (ECI) website, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is currently leading in 192 seats, while the Trinamool Congress (TMC) is ahead in 94 seats. The trends continue to shift as counting progresses, with final results still awaited. Get Latest News Live on Times Now along with Breaking News and Top Headlines from Viral and around the World.
